items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: But what he did for Professor Longhair, this is when I really found out that he's a good man. You see, Professor Longhair was taken.

ctx.x: But he is basically a good man. And you can go there and get any information you want. But I do know one thing. He's just in part of the thing. He's part of the clique. And there ain't nothing much he can do. But what he did for Professor Longhair, this is when I really found out that he's a good man. You see, Professor Longhair was taken. The Fess was taken. And when Mr. Weinstein found out about it, and he took over Fess's business, that's why whatever Professor Longhair had right now today is because of Mr.…
What about your dealings with 496 over the years? What did you do about it?

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: he was one of these piano players like Professor Longhead. He played as well as Professor Longhead.

ctx.x: Yeah, did, you talk about music in the neighborhood, and people visiting. Did people in those days sit down on their porches and play music?

What high it was, the houses that had pianos in them. See, most houses, any way people that had any kind of little money, they would all have a piano in the house. Mm-hmm. And, uh, my uncle, uh, Robert Wilson, he's a minister, he used to, he was one of these piano players like Professor Longhead. He played as well as Professor Longhead. Right. In fact, my uncle, my cousin, Joe Mitchell, he just died about, about, I'd say, two months ago. Now, this is his words. He'd say, ah, and that guy, he's talking about…

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: And that's how myself, Professor Longhair, quite a few other people.

ctx.x: Yeah. First of all, Jerry Wexler was the type of man at that time. And from what I can gather, he hasn't changed. I used to call Jerry Wexler. I'd get on my phone and call Jerry Wexler. Me and him talk just like we talk. I could never do that with Luchette. In fact, I think I remember seeing Luchette once. But Wexler was, that's why they were so successful, I think. He was ideal. Everybody liked him. He found out they had talent in New Orleans and every week. Jerry Wexler and Armand Erdogan, he was down here. And…
Yeah, something I wanted to say. You told me, we talked about this last time, you actually got statements from Atlanta.
